summary: A reels-famous forest cascade between Ahwa and Don — a waterfall that exists mostly as a map pin, monsoon videos and word of mouth.
description:
Birsa is the definition of a pinch-in spot: zoom the map between Ahwa and Don and a waterfall pin appears, backed by a steady stream of monsoon reels and very little else. The videos show a broad, forceful cascade in green forest — clearly worth a stop on the Don road in season — but published facts (exact village, path length, safe viewing points) are thin to nonexistent.

This record exists to be ground-truthed. If you go: it sits roughly fourteen kilometres from Don on the Ahwa side, monsoon-only, with no facilities and no management. Ask in the villages along the road, take the usual Dang precautions, and treat every detail here as provisional until someone paces it out.
highlights: Roadside-belt cascade on the Ahwa–Don stretch

modes.road: On or just off the Ahwa–Don road; ask locally for the current pull-off

access.last_mile: Short walk from the road by most accounts — unverified
access.road_condition: Interior tar; the Don stretch beyond is rough

experience.photography_notes: The reels favour the head-on road-side angle in August spate.

amenities.food: None — Ahwa is the supply stop

warnings: Unmanaged monsoon water — keep off wet rock shelves and out of the flow
Details here are provisional; scout before committing children or elders

tips: Fold into the Don day — waterfall, plateau and Don falls make one loop
If you ground-truth it, note the village name and path — this record needs it

seo.meta_description: Birsa waterfall between Ahwa and Don: what the monsoon reels show, what remains unverified, and how to attempt it.
